facts.raw_span: A 28-year-old G2P1 woman presented 31 days after an elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia
with worsening headache and easy fatigability for 3 days
The headache was continuous, global, and had become severe over 24 hours
associated with nausea and malaise
Eight days postoperatively she had developed a mild global headache managed with rest and paracetamol
By day 31 the headache was severe, nonpositional, and unrelieved by rest or analgesics
Vital signs were normal
She was fully conscious and oriented
all meningeal signs were negative
motor function was intact
Laboratory studies showed a normal complete blood count, prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio

Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection over the left frontoparietal convexity with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity, measuring 15 mm in width with a 13-mm midline shift

concepts.why: The noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection, which is consistent with a subdural hematoma.
The patient presented with a worsening headache 31 days after an elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia, which is a common cause of post-dural puncture headache.

The patient's headache was severe, nonpositional, and unrelieved by rest or analgesics, and the CT scan revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection, which is consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma.
The CT scan revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection, which could also be consistent with an epidural hematoma.
The patient presented with a severe headache, nausea, and malaise, which could be consistent with cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
Although the patient's meningeal signs were negative, the presence of a severe headache and fever could still be consistent with meningitis.
The patient presented with a worsening headache and easy fatigability, which could be consistent with a tension headache.
The patient presented with a headache 31 days after an elective cesarean delivery, which could be consistent with a postpartum headache.

rationales.F01: The patient's recent cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia increases the likelihood of post-dural puncture headache.
rationales.F02: The worsening headache suggests a possible complication related to the spinal anesthesia or the postpartum period.
rationales.F05: The development of a mild global headache eight days postoperatively, which was managed with rest and paracetamol, could be an early sign of a post-dural puncture headache or another postpartum complication.
rationales.F09: The absence of meningeal signs decreases the likelihood of meningitis.
rationales.F12: The noncontrast CT of the head revealing a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection is highly suggestive of a subdural hematoma, particularly a chronic one given the time frame.
